com.snaptrade:snaptrade-java-sdk 6.0.22 发布, Connect brokerage accounts to your app for live positions and trading.  ## Rate limiting  Two limits apply to requests signed with your `clientId`. The stricter one wins, and exceeding either returns `429 Too Many Requests`.  - **Customer-level** — 250 requests/minute by default, scoped to your   `clientId` and applied across all endpoints. Reported in   `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. - **Account-level** — 10 requests/minute per account, scoped to   (`clientId`, `accountId`). All covered operations for one account draw on   the same bucket — reading balances and reading positions share it — and   enforcement does not depend on the HTTP method, so updating an account   consumes the same bucket as reading it. Only enforced for Personal users,   and only for integrations it has been rolled out to — it is not yet in   force for every Personal integration. It also does not apply on every   operation that documents a 429 below. Where it applies it is reported in   `X-RateLimit-Account-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Account-Remaining` and   `X-RateLimit-Account-Reset`. Do not read the absence of those headers as   proof the limit is off — some configurations omit the rate limit headers   while still enforcing the limit, so header absence tells you nothing   about your allowance.  On a 429, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` means you hit the customer-level limit and `X-RateLimit-Account-Remaining: 0` means the account-level one. Wait for the corresponding `*-Reset` value (seconds) before retrying, or fall back to exponential backoff with jitter.  Not every 429 is explained by those headers. A separate per-authenticated-user limit, reported in no `X-RateLimit-*` header, covers OAuth-authenticated requests and signed requests in configurations where the customer-level limit is not in effect — on the operations that use the default throttles. A few operations override those and are governed by the customer-level limit alone. The two do not stack: a signed request governed by the customer-level limit above is not additionally subject to the per-user one. If a 429 arrives with no header at zero — or with no `X-RateLimit-*` headers at all — honour `Retry-After` and back off. Treat the remaining counts as a hint, not a guarantee that the next request will succeed.  Because the customer-level limit applies everywhere, any signed request can return 429.  **OAuth-authenticated requests are an exception.** They are not subject to the customer-level limit and do not receive `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` or `X-RateLimit-Reset` — do not wait on those headers or design around a customer-level allowance on this path. The account-level limit still applies to them on the account-data endpoints above, reported in the `X-RateLimit-Account-*` headers. On operations using the default throttles the per-user limit above applies to them as well, so an OAuth request can be rejected while the account headers still show capacity; on the few operations that override those throttles, OAuth callers have no per-user ceiling at all. Drive retries from `Retry-After` and exponential backoff with jitter rather than from the headers.  See https://docs.snaptrade.com/docs/ratelimiting.

        plugin actually runs.

        Everything else is tested by calling the generator directly, which never proves the
        Mojo can be configured, that the language target is found through ServiceLoader out
        of a plugin classloader, that the output directory is registered as a test source
        root, or that generated code compiles against models a real openapi-generator
        emitted rather than ones written by hand to look like it.

        It replaces an integration-test module that contained nothing but a pom. Being an
        example rather than a test suite is the point: it has to stay readable, which is a
        harder constraint than passing, and it is what a newcomer will copy.

        test jar, which read as "the core's fixture, borrowed". It is not: it is the one
        specification every layer is measured against, and each layer has an equal claim on
        it. A module of its own says that, and removes the test-jar dependency that only
        existed to carry a single file.

        A test aid, not a product artifact: built and installed so the reactor can use it,
        never deployed.

org.monflabs.nashorn:nashorn-node 2026.0.0 发布, EXPERIMENTAL, INCOMPLETE. A Node-compatibility module resolver, provided as
    a convenience and as a worked example of building built-in modules on the
    engine. Answers a handful of Node's built-in specifiers - fs, buffer, os,
    path - from bare or node: imports, in pure Java. It reaches into the
    engine's internal object model (core exports those packages to this module
    by name), so a given nashorn-node is a companion to the exact same version of
    nashorn-core; do not mix versions.

ai.mattmann.mnemosyne:cas-metadata 1.13.2 发布, A Multi-valued, generic Metadata container class. The class uses an internal
	Map of string keys pointing to vectors of strings. The data
	structure looks like the following:

	[std:string key]⇒std:vector of std:strings

	The multi-valued nature of the class is handled transparently by this Metadata
	container. Since all values are stored internally as string vectors, the difference
	between a scalar value and a non-scalar is handled by determining whether the list of
	values for a particular key is greater than 1.

items.title: ai.bithuman:essence2-android 0.5.10 发布, Android AAR for the bitHuman essence-2 avatar engine: drives an avatar bundle and composes teeth BORROWED from the donor bank rather than synthesizing them. A self-hosted session is metered at the published self-hosted rate (https://docs.bithuman.ai/guides/pricing); a credential the service rejects keeps rendering for a five-minute grace, then the session refuses, while a service that cannot be reached never stops a render. Bundles the engine's native library plus libonnxruntime.so and libc++_shared.so for arm64-v8a.

        drop-in plugin bundles (PLAT-12). A thin, zero-additional-dependency validator: it
        depends only on ravenroot-application-api, reusing PayloadJson/PayloadValue/PayloadLimits
        for manifest parsing rather than adding a YAML or JSON Schema library. Deliberately does
        not depend on ravenroot-core: this module never loads a class, never touches
        NodePackage/NodePackages, and is callable standalone by plugin.sh (build/validate/install)
        without pulling in the runtime.

items.title:
ai.ravenroot:ravenroot-observability-otel 0.4.1-alpha.1 发布, PLAT-01: the OpenTelemetry export bridge, spans, metrics and
        log-correlation identifiers derived from ai.ravenroot.api.application.ExecutionEvent, the
        same event ai.ravenroot.server.audit.StructuredExecutionLogger already consumes. Depends on
        ravenroot-application-api (the event shape) and ravenroot-core (ExecutionMonitor.subscribe,
        the only extension point this module uses) and nothing else in the ai.ravenroot tree. Neither
        of those two modules, nor ravenroot-application-api's other consumers, every third-party
        node package, depends on this one: the OpenTelemetry SDK is reachable from exactly one kind
        of caller, a composition root (RavenrootServerMain, RavenrootCliMain), which is what makes
        "no OpenTelemetry dependency in core" a property the compiler enforces rather than prose.
        Disabled unless RAVENROOT_OTEL_ENABLED is set; see
        TelemetryConfiguration. Every OpenTelemetry artifact here is Apache License 2.0; this module
        has not been through the release SBOM and licence scan and should be before it
        ships in a tagged release.
